newsitem.title: USA: Ford not assuming Q1 cost-cut rate to continue.
newsitem.headline: Ford not assuming Q1 cost-cut rate to continue.

text.p: Ford Motor Co chief financial officer John Devine said Wednesday the automaker is not assuming its $800 million cost-savings rate in the first quarter will continue through the year.
"We're not ready to assume that for the full year," Devine told reporters at a news conference here. "I don't want you to multiply that ($800 million) by four."
Ford, which has a goal of $1 billion in cost cuts in 1997, moved some cost cutting measures to earlier in the year, Devine said.
Devine also said the company sees the auto industry environment in 1997 to be about the same as 1996, with a strong first quarter sales pace that is not sustained through the year.
"I think the interesting thing about '97 is it's beginning to look a lot like '96," Devine said.

Ford, which endured interrupted production of its popular Expedition sport/utility vehicle and Econoline van due to a strike by a seat supplier in the first quarter, will make up that lost production in the second quarter, Devine said.
Ford also said it was confident of achieving its target of a four percent return on automotive sales in the North American market in 1997, after posting a 5.1 percent return in the first quarter.
"We feel fairly confident about making that target," Devine said.

But in terms of having a profitable year in Europe, one of the company's goals, Devine was more hesitant, despite posting net income of $105 million on that continent in the first quarter, up from $73 million a year ago.
"We're not out of the woods in Europe yet," Devine said. "We have a lot of work to do."
The first half of the year in Europe is typically stronger than the second half, Devine said.
Separately, Devine said credit losses are expected to continue to be a drag on its Ford Credit unit earnings for the year.
